common_name: Purity Candytuft (Classic Evergreen White-Flowered Perennial Candytuft)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Purity is a classic evergreen perennial candytuft producing a dense mat of glossy dark green foliage smothered in pure white flowers in spring.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; excellent drainage is essential, since candytuft quickly declines in heavy, wet soil. Purity is a classic, widely grown perennial candytuft producing a dense, low, spreading mat of glossy, dark evergreen foliage that provides year-round structure at the front of a border or in a rock garden, completely smothered each spring in masses of small, pure white flowers. It is drought-tolerant once established and tolerates poor, rocky soil well, making it a reliable, low-maintenance edging plant. Shear the mat back lightly after flowering to keep growth dense and compact and to encourage the best bloom the following spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Snowflake produces unusually large individual flowers and broader foliage compared to older candytuft cultivars, giving a bolder spring display.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; sharp drainage is essential, since candytuft declines quickly in heavy, wet soil. Snowflake is a robust perennial candytuft selection with larger individual flowers and broader, more substantial evergreen foliage than many older cultivars, creating an especially bold, dense carpet of white bloom in spring. It provides good year-round structure as a low evergreen groundcover for the front of a border or rock garden, and tolerates poor, rocky soil and drought well once established. Shear back lightly after flowering to maintain a dense, compact habit and encourage strong bloom the following year.

common_name: Little Gem Candytuft (Compact Dwarf Evergreen Candytuft)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Little Gem is a compact, dwarf candytuft selection well suited to rock gardens and small-space edging where larger candytuft cultivars would spread too wide.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; excellent drainage is essential, since candytuft declines quickly in heavy, wet soil. Little Gem is a dwarf, compact perennial candytuft selection that stays smaller and neater than most cultivars, forming a tight, low mound of glossy evergreen foliage well suited to rock gardens, trough plantings, and tight edging where a spreading, larger candytuft would take up too much space. It produces the same clean white spring flowers typical of the species over its compact mound, and tolerates poor, rocky soil and drought well once established. Shear back lightly after flowering to keep the mound tidy and encourage the best bloom the following spring.

common_name: Snowflake Creeping Phlox (Pure White Moss Phlox)

planting.note: Plant container plants in late winter or early spring in well-drained to dry, slightly alkaline to neutral, sandy or rocky soil in full sun; moss phlox performs best in sharply drained, lean soil, since rich, moist soil promotes lush foliage at the expense of flowering.

directions: Plant in well-drained, sandy or rocky, lean soil in full sun. Snowflake is a pure white-flowered selection of moss phlox, forming a dense, low, needle-textured evergreen mat that becomes completely smothered in small white flowers for several weeks in early spring, one of the classic rock garden and slope groundcovers for that season. It thrives in the same sharply drained, lean, sunny conditions that suit other moss phlox cultivars, struggling in rich, wet soil, and works beautifully cascading over a rock wall or covering a sunny bank. Shear the mat back lightly after flowering to keep the foliage dense and encourage strong bloom the following spring.

common_name: Purple Beauty Creeping Phlox (Rich Violet-Purple Moss Phlox)

planting.note: Plant container plants in late winter or early spring in well-drained to dry, slightly alkaline to neutral, sandy or rocky soil in full sun; moss phlox performs best in sharply drained, lean soil, since rich, moist soil promotes lush foliage at the expense of flowering.

directions: Plant in well-drained, sandy or rocky, lean soil in full sun. Purple Beauty is a richly colored moss phlox selection producing an especially vivid, deep violet-purple spring flower display over a dense, low, evergreen, needle-textured mat, one of the more saturated colors available among moss phlox cultivars. Like other moss phlox it thrives in sharply drained, lean, sunny sites and struggles in rich, wet soil, making it an excellent choice for a rock garden, sunny slope, or cascading over a retaining wall. Shear the mat back lightly after flowering to maintain dense growth and encourage the strongest bloom the following year.
